scope: Standalone one-entry load/store address and attribute preparation. No connection to the production IQ/ROB, data bus, LSQ, forwarding, load-return extension or store retirement; no full-core memory acceptance or physical timing claim.
handshake: launch_i is an accepted launch, qualified by ready_o. A registered descriptor holds until take_i; accepted take plus launch replaces it without a bubble. Reset/full flush suppress ready and valid immediately and discard the holder. All descriptor outputs are zero while invalid. Selective recovery must qualify flush against the held full ROB identity externally.
decode: Caller supplies only legal LB/LH/LW/LBU/LHU/SB/SH/SW instructions and an aligned PC. The shared decode and execution blocks compute RV32 base plus signed immediate modulo 2^32, natural-alignment faults before PMA access faults, and mtval=effective address. x0 input payloads are forced to zero, and loads consume no second source. The pinned platform regions have naturally aligned boundaries for all supported sizes; this stage does not add arbitrary split-region accesses.
descriptor: Preserve full 13-bit ROB generation/slot identity, original instruction/PC, architectural operands, effective byte address, size (0 byte, 1 halfword, 2 word), store and unsigned-load flags. byte_mask_o indexes bytes of the containing aligned 32-bit word. Store data is shifted into those word lanes and masked; loads and all faults have zero write_data. Faults have zero byte mask and uncached flag. These fields are metadata, not a valid memory request or a retirement event.
ordering: Successful cacheable idempotent loads have head_only=0, which is eligibility only: older-store hazards and permissions still govern issue. All stores, uncached/non-idempotent loads and faults have head_only=1. A consumer must never expose store bytes or access MMIO merely because the descriptor is accepted. Cache/LSQ, data-port ownership and atomic store/ROB retirement are separate later tasks.
